title: Gamaliel Cordoba takes oath as Supreme Court associate justice
summary: Gamaliel Cordoba took his oath on Thursday as the new Supreme Court (SC) Associate Justice, succeeding Associate Justice Amy Lazaro-Javier, who retired on November 16, 2026.

blocks.text: Gamaliel Cordoba took his oath on Thursday as the new Supreme Court (SC) Associate Justice, succeeding Associate Justice Amy Lazaro-Javier, who retired on November 16, 2026.
He took his oath before Chief Justice Rodil Zalameda at the High Court's Session Hall.
Prior to his appointment, Cordoba served as the chairperson of the Commission on Audit (COA), having been appointed by President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. on October 21, 2022.
During his time at COA, the agency submitted at least 50 fraud audit reports to the Office of the Ombudsman and the Independent Commission for Infrastructure.
He also institutionalized GPS-based geotagging of all government infrastructure projects nationwide to ensure proper verification of project status.

Upon the announcement of Cordoba's appointment, Malacañang said that reassigning a leader to a different agency does not signify a loss of the President's trust; instead he sees their potential to do even better in the new role.

"Nakikita ng Pangulo sino yung mga taong nararapat na makasama at manatili sa administrasyon. Nakikita niya kung ano yung kanilang mga potensyal. Nakitaan niya ng kagalingan so ilalagay niya sa mga pwesto na mas kakailanganin pa ang kanilang galing," Palace Press Officer Undersecretary Claire Castro said in a press briefing.
(The President knows who is deserving to join and stay in the administration. He sees their potential. If he sees their potential, he will place them in agencies where they show their abilities.)
Cordoba also served the longest term as commissioner of the National Telecommunications Commission (NTC), serving under four administrations from 2009-2022.
From 2008 to 2009, Cordoba also served on the Board of Directors of the Philippine Amusement and Gaming Corporation (PAGCOR).
He also held several key positions under the Arroyo administration at the Office of the President.
Cordoba obtained his Bachelor of Arts in Economics in 1992 and Juris Doctor in 1996 at the Ateneo de Manila University. —LDF, GMA News
